$comment: How Agent Cake sorts and judges sessions, in one place. 'verdicts' is the first level, one per session (the API's verdict and the session list's filters); 'unsure' names a stretch the behavior model could not tell (bars, timelines, layers: never a verdict); 'evidence' marks a Human session AgentCake could not tell (no Unknown: such a session counts as human, marked); 'turns' splits an Agent session into Agent only and Human + agent (cake's classes agent and mixed); 'names' says which agent: how sure a product's or an automation tool's name is, or Unnamed when no name fits, shown beside the name (the kind of agent, the verdict's Agent row, and where it runs are reasons, never a category: agentcake/detect/attribute.py; there are no kinds of agent). The dashboard's categories block lists the verdicts and the split, and only those. The local pages read these labels and sentences when they are built (web/vite.config.ts), the API's words (titles, the coverage note) when it answers. 'classes' says how each class of agentcake/detect/verdict.py is decided, as the coverage note's 'how it's decided' column shows it, and 'named' how an agent's name is found; 'when_model_runs' is the rule of agentcake/detect/schedule.py, its {quiet} and {interval} filled from the settings judge_quiet_s and judge_interval_ms (public_judge_interval_ms on a server). Interface text: English only; visitors are Human or Agent, never person, people or user.
title: Session categories
lead: Each session gets one of these verdicts.

human.label: Human
human.about: Only a human acted. Sessions that can't be classified also count as Human and get the Thin evidence tag.

agent.label: Agent
agent.about: An AI agent or automation acted, from start to finish or taking turns with a human.

bot.label: Bot
bot.about: The visitor is a program on the bot list, such as a search engine or a monitor, not an agent. Bots are only counted.

unsure.label: Unknown
unsure.about: The behavior model couldn't classify this part of the session. Unknown isn't a session verdict: the verdict uses only the parts the model could classify.

thin.label: Thin evidence
thin.about: The session counts as Human because it has too few actions, comes from a phone or tablet, or has evidence that's too weak or points both ways. Its reasons say which applies.

agent_only.label: Agent only
agent_only.about: An agent acted from start to finish in this Agent session.

human_agent.label: Human + agent
human_agent.about: A human and an agent took turns in this Agent session. The timeline marks each hand-off.

verified.label: Verified
verified.about: A signature or a published address range confirms the name.

likely.label: Likely
likely.about: The visitor reports the name, or the product leaves its own traces in the page.

possible.label: Possible
possible.about: Only its behavior points to the product.

unnamed.label: Unnamed
unnamed.about: No product or tool name matches the evidence. The reasons say what was seen.

human.how: There are no automation traces and no agent name, and the behavior model judges the actions to be human.

agent_ai.how: There are agent traces in the page or the browser, and the behavior model judges the actions to be an agent's. Traces include an extension acting on the page or a cloud computer's fixed setup. The name comes from a verified signature, the product's own traces, or the User-Agent.

agent_automated.how: The browser shows automation markers, such as webdriver, a headless browser, or requests without a language header. The behavior model splits the session into stretches. Crawler-like patterns only go into the reasons.

bot.how: The User-Agent or a signature matches the list of programs that aren't agents. It's marked “Verified” when a published address range or a signature confirms it. The behavior model doesn't run.

mixed.how: The behavior model finds both a human and an agent in the same session and marks the hand-off where the actions change.

too_little_data.how: There are fewer actions than the behavior model needs, or the visit comes from a phone or tablet, so no guess is made. A setting controls how many actions the model needs.

not_sure.how: The evidence is too weak or points both ways. Examples include a trace that open DevTools also leave and keyboard navigation like an assistive tool's.

excluded.how: A page the browser loaded in advance but never showed (a prefetch or prerender)

named.how: The User-Agent contains a name, or a verified signature names the visitor. The behavior model still splits the session into stretches.

when_model_runs: The behavior model runs on this computer when new data arrives, at most every {interval} while a session keeps sending.
When a session has been quiet for {quiet}, the model judges it once more and its verdict becomes final. New data opens it again.
Opening a replay or the dashboard triggers another judgment of sessions with new data.
Bots known by name and sessions with too few actions don't go through the model.
Nothing is sent to any AI service or over the network.
